operator: The deposit screen's classifier (services/backend/src/reveal_backend/deposit_screen.py). Nothing here is pinned yet: revision, source_files and files are filled in once by an operator, and an image is not built until they are.

1. Licence: the model is gated. Accept the Llama 4 Community License on https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-Prompt-Guard-2-22M with the Hugging Face account whose token will fetch it, and keep the licence terms with the deployment.

2. Converter: in a separate virtual environment, never the image or REVEAL's .venv, install the ONNX exporter: python3 -m venv /tmp/pg-convert && /tmp/pg-convert/bin/pip install 'optimum-onnx[onnxruntime]' torch transformers. Point REVEAL_PROMPT_GUARD_CONVERTER at /tmp/pg-convert/bin/optimum-cli (default: optimum-cli on PATH).

3. Pin: HF_TOKEN=<read token> python scripts/platform_bundle.py <output> --fetch-assets --allow-dirty --pin-prompt-guard. It resolves the repository's current commit, downloads that revision into .deployment-assets/prompt-guard-2-22m/, converts it to ONNX with conversion.command, and writes the revision, the sha256 of every downloaded file (source_files) and of every file the image carries (files) into this lock. Review the diff and commit it.

4. Later fetches (no --pin-prompt-guard) reuse .deployment-assets/prompt-guard-2-22m/ when it matches files; otherwise they download the pinned revision, refuse any file whose sha256 differs from source_files, convert, and refuse a conversion whose files differ from files (ONNX export is not byte-reproducible across converter versions: keep the folder, or re-pin).

5. Measure on the 1-vCPU task before relying on the screen: deposit_screen logs nothing per window, but job_metrics records each screen's windows and seconds (admin telemetry). Target under 50 ms per 512-token window and under 5 s per job with a few full papers.
HF_TOKEN is read from the environment by the fetch only. It is never written to the bundle, the image, a log or this file.
